A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KV cache compression study and ShotKV method. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression experiments across fundamental capabilities, attention analyses, and ShotKV results on many-shot GSM8K and LongGenBench-GSM8K.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds attention-distribution measurements, Mistral evaluations, broader ShotKV results, and latency/throughput measurements.

M1.justification: ShotKV retains the same shot scoring, budget-constrained prefill selection, fixed compressed prefill cache, and dynamic decoding-token selection. Equations (2)-(9) and Algorithm 1 match. v2 clarifies which queries supply attention weights without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, CommonsenseQA, GSM8K, HumanEval, JailBreakV and LongGenBench, including many-shot arithmetic reasoning. KVFundaBench names the existing suite. The additional model evaluations and efficiency measurements do not establish new datasets, domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: The matched task/many-shot comparisons retain StreamingLLM, H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV and ChunkKV; LongGenBench retains StreamingLLM, H2O and PyramidInfer, alongside FullKV. Adding ShotKV results to Figure 5 introduces no new competing method. Newly cited SCOPE is not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds Mistral-7B-Instruct evaluation at five compression ratios and latency/throughput testing with batch size 1, 4096 or 8192 input tokens, and 4096 output tokens. Existing task metrics, shot counts, temperature zero and LongGenBench parameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 3.2 adds a controlled cumulative-attention analysis including versus excluding the first four sink tokens, extending v1's qualitative heatmaps. Appendices B.3 and C.2 add a model-family generality check and sequence-length-dependent efficiency analysis. These substantially extend the supplementary evidence while retaining the earlier sensitivity studies.

E5.justification: Both versions describe confidence intervals around performance averaged across five compression methods. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence-level specification, significance testing or new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 5 adds ShotKV curves across the fundamental tasks; Figures 3 and 9 add attention-distribution and Mistral results. Table 11 newly reports, for 8192 input and 4096 output tokens, FullKV versus ShotKV latency of 183.42 versus 162.78 seconds and throughput of 55.93 versus 63.24 tokens/s. Matched earlier tables retain their values; percentage conversions are equivalent representations.

T1.justification: The compression definitions, relative-performance formula, shot-selection objective and constraint, and scoring equations are retained. The added attention-weight explanation clarifies existing notation; no new theorem, proof, derivation or substantive mathematical revision appears.

C1.justification: v2 presents the existing evaluation suite as the named benchmark KVFundaBench and makes it a principal contribution, while dropping v1's explicit first-comprehensive-study claim. The central compression-sensitivity findings and claimed ShotKV advantages remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains arithmetic sensitivity through more diffuse non-sink attention and adds interpretations concerning model-family generality and practical inference efficiency. Observation 5 now explicitly attributes prompting gains to CoT. v1's specific deployment/training recommendations are removed, while its benchmark and resource limitations are retained in Appendix F.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 specifies the queries used for prefill and decoding attention scores. v2 also documents LongGenBench's 23,000 examples and supplies hardware, batch size and sequence lengths for the efficiency test. Conversely, Figure 2 drops v1's explicit LLaMA layer-15/head-10 identification.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Mistral 7B and SCOPE, explicitly acknowledging SCOPE's prefill-decoding separation strategy. Most related-work coverage is retained and moved into Appendix A; citation-style changes do not represent additional research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, ShotKV motivation and conclusion are extensively rewritten around KVFundaBench and named observations. Related work moves to the appendix, attention analysis becomes a dedicated subsection, Further Discussion disappears, and the appendices gain a contents page and separate impact/limitations sections.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with widespread figure/table resizing, relocation and relabeling. v2 adds Figures 3 and 9 and Tables 1 and 11, rearranges the main performance panels and adds ShotKV curves. Its Figure 8 also clips the low one-shot endpoint displayed in v1 Figure 6.

improvement.justification: The sink-token control strengthens the attention-based explanation, Mistral evaluation checks another model family, and measured latency/throughput supplies practical evidence absent from v1. Clearer attention-scoring details also help reproducibility. These provide a limited net gain: the efficiency test leaves its model and compression ratio unspecified, statistical documentation is unchanged, and the revised shot-count plot clips an important endpoint.
